According to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, Apple is developing several new features for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, which will be more appealing to health-conscious users. The company is reportedly also testing two finishes for the rumoured ceramic version.

Brand New Health Upgrades

If you are not satisfied with the Apple Watch's performance as a fitness tracker, the following two key health upgrades should catch your eye. The two features are all-day heart rate monitoring and a completely redesigned app that makes it easier for you to extract useful information from your health data. Here is Gurman's description of the new app:

As a current WHOOP user, I would say its biggest appeal to me has always been that the WHOOP app makes it easier for me to extract useful information from health data. It shows me the various factors affecting sleep or recovery, but the Apple Watch seems to focus only on the three activity rings. If Apple makes meaningful progress in this area, I would be quite pleased.

The key to a richer Apple Watch experience lies in having more data. Apple is reportedly testing continuous all-day recording with the heart rate sensor, rather than only during workouts or random sampling.

Two New Finishes

We have previously heard that Apple is considering adding a ceramic material to the Apple Watch Series 12, and Gurman now reports there will be two colour options: the traditional white, and a dark grey. There will also be "several new watch band colours and configurations."

A Redesign is Coming in the Future

The current Apple Watch design language was introduced in 2024 with the Apple Watch Series 12. That was a relatively mild change, as the company made the watch slimmer by narrowing the bezel. According to Bloomberg, next year's Series 13 may feature a new Apple Watch redesign, though it may also be pushed back to the Series 14:

I am quite looking forward to Apple's new work. They seem to have nearly reached the limit of the rounded design language, so perhaps we will see a completely new look. Hopefully it will not affect compatibility with older watch bands.
